you have low coverage samples and there is also and error message about the SAM file format, make sure the format of the files resembles the ones in the examples in the package
https://code.google.com/p/methylkit/source/browse/inst/extdata/test.fastq_bismark.sorted.min.sam

it is not easy to suggest a solution where we can't replicate the problem. You need to find out on your own by trial and error what files are giving the error, and if the error relates to file format or low coverage. General suggestions are that the data is low coverage and bases are either filtered on coverage or quality thresholds and the program exits without being able calculate conversion rate. The second error suggests a file format issue, make sure the file format is correct.

The last solution I can suggest is to use Bismark scripts to output a per base methylation information including coverage and methylation ratios. There are some scripts in the latest bismark that can do that, and try to format and read that file into methylKit.

Best,
Altuna

I would also suggest you check base qualities from your samples. If they are systematically low, it indicates a problem with your samples.

For your question you need to process the files you get from Bismark to a format that is acceptable by methylKit. Please see the blog posts on this:
http://zvfak.blogspot.de/2012/10/how-to-read-bsmap-methylation-ratio.html
http://zvfak.blogspot.de/2013/03/using-encode-methylation-data-rrbs-in-r.html

The minimal information needed is as follows:
chr,start,end,strand,coverage and ratio of methylation

Example of such a file would be something like this

chr1 12323 - 10 0.1
chr1 22423 + 90 0.76
chr1 32333 + 200 0.83

and this is how you would read the file:
library(methylKit)
obj = read("example.file.txt",
                 sample.id = "test", assembly = "hg19", header = FALSE, 
                 context = "CpG", resolution = "base", 
                 pipeline = list(fraction = TRUE, chr.col = 1, start.col = 2, 
                                  end.col = 2,coverage.col = 4, strand.col = 3, 
                                  freqC.col = 5))


you have to select for CG context and do some arithmetics on the columns of the "Genome wide cytosin report" to get percent/ratio of methylation and coverage values.
This doable via a small perl script or maybe even awk one liner. If you know your way around some scripting language this shouldn't take more than 10 minutes to write.

Best,
Altuna

On Monday, November 10, 2014 10:57:15 AM UTC+1, Altuna Akalin wrote:
I would also suggest you check base qualities from your samples. If they are systematically low, it indicates a problem with your samples.

For your question you need to process the files you get from Bismark to a format that is acceptable by methylKit. Please see the blog posts on this:
http://zvfak.blogspot.de/2012/10/how-to-read-bsmap-methylation-ratio.html
http://zvfak.blogspot.de/2013/03/using-encode-methylation-data-rrbs-in-r.html

The minimal information needed is as follows:
chr,start,end,strand,coverage and ratio of methylation

Example of such a file would be something like this

chr1 12323 - 10 0.1
chr1 22423 + 90 0.76
chr1 32333 + 200 0.83

and this is how you would read the file:
library(methylKit)
obj = read("example.file.txt",
                 sample.id = "test", assembly = "hg19", header = FALSE, 
                 context = "CpG", resolution = "base", 
                 pipeline = list(fraction = TRUE, chr.col = 1, start.col = 2, 
                                  end.col = 2,coverage.col = 4, strand.col = 3, 
                                  freqC.col = 5))


you have to select for CG context and do some arithmetics on the columns of the "Genome wide cytosin report" to get percent/ratio of methylation and coverage values.
This doable via a small perl script or maybe even awk one liner. If you know your way around some scripting language this shouldn't take more than 10 minutes to write.

Best,
Altuna

On Friday, November 7, 2014 2:19:48 PM UTC+1, Altuna Akalin wrote:
you have low coverage samples and there is also and error message about the SAM file format, make sure the format of the files resembles the ones in the examples in the package
https://code.google.com/p/methylkit/source/browse/inst/extdata/test.fastq_bismark.sorted.min.sam

it is not easy to suggest a solution where we can't replicate the problem. You need to find out on your own by trial and error what files are giving the error, and if the error relates to file format or low coverage. General suggestions are that the data is low coverage and bases are either filtered on coverage or quality thresholds and the program exits without being able calculate conversion rate. The second error suggests a file format issue, make sure the file format is correct.

The last solution I can suggest is to use Bismark scripts to output a per base methylation information including coverage and methylation ratios. There are some scripts in the latest bismark that can do that, and try to format and read that file into methylKit.

Best,
Altuna
